title: Each tab saves its own stale copy of the whole list, so a second tab erases the first tab's recipes
evidence: The list is read once at load and the whole array is written on every change (app.js:23-24, 34-35). There is no 'storage' listener and no re-read before a write. Driven with two pages open on the same origin: tab 1 added X, tab 2 added Y; localStorage ended as only [{"name":"Y"...}].
failing_case: Open the app in two tabs. Add 'X' in tab 1, then add 'Y' in tab 2. Storage now holds only Y; X is lost, and tab 1 still shows X until it is reloaded.
remediation: Re-read storage (loadRecipes) immediately before each mutation and write the merged list, and listen to the 'storage' event to refresh the view.

quote: return [];  // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Corrupt saved data is swallowed, never reported, and overwritten by the next save
evidence: store.js:8-10 returns [] for any parse error. The comment says app.js tells the user, but app.js never checks why the list is empty (grep for any message on load: none). Driven in Chromium: with localStorage 'recipes' set to a truncated JSON string, the page shows 'No recipes yet', the status is empty, and after one add the stored value is replaced by only the new recipe. Line 7 also drops, with no notice, every record whose name is not a string; the next save erases them from storage.
failing_case: A user's saved list is damaged (partial write, hand edit, another version's shape). They open the page and see the empty state with no warning. They add one recipe. localStorage 'recipes' becomes [{"name":"New",...}] and the original raw text, which could have been repaired, is gone for good.
remediation: Make loadRecipes return {list, error}. On a parse failure, copy the raw string to a backup key before anything is written, and show a status that names the problem and the backup. Do not save over unreadable data.

title: Valid number-input values like '1e2' are saved as the wrong time (1 minute)
evidence: A type=number input accepts '1e2' (checkValidity() returned true in Chromium, min 1, max 600). parseInt('1e2', 10) is 1. Driven: submitting '1e2' saved the row 'Soup 1 min' and the status 'Total cooking time: 1 minutes.' No error was shown.
failing_case: User types 1e2 (or 6e1) in Minutes and presses Save recipe. The browser accepts it as 100, the app stores 1 and reports it as saved. The same truncation hides any other string that parseInt cuts short.
remediation: Parse with Number(value) (or valueAsNumber), then require Number.isInteger and 1 <= n <= 600 in one validator that the form handler and loadRecipes both use.

title: Delete ignores a failed save and still says 'Deleted'
evidence: The add path checks the boolean from saveRecipes (app.js:24-25); the delete path drops it. Driven: with Storage.prototype.setItem throwing, clicking Delete and confirming set the status to 'Deleted “A”.' and removed the row; after a reload the recipe was back.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked. The user deletes a recipe, sees 'Deleted “A”.' and the row vanishes. On the next visit the recipe is back. The message reported a failure as success.
remediation: Use the return value as the add path does: if saveRecipes returns false, say the delete was not saved and why, and either restore the row or keep it marked as pending.

title: After a keyboard delete, focus drops to the page body
evidence: render() replaces list.innerHTML, so the focused Delete button is destroyed. Driven: focus the first Delete, press Enter, accept the confirm; document.activeElement was BODY. The status line is announced, but the keyboard position is lost.
failing_case: A keyboard user deletes the first of ten recipes. Focus resets to the top of the document, so they must tab through the form and the list again to reach the next Delete (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order).
remediation: After render(), focus the next row's Delete button (or the previous one, or the 'Your recipes' heading with tabindex=-1 when the list is empty).

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: Loader only checks name; records with string, missing or non-finite minutes poison the total and the list
evidence: totalMinutes (store.js:23) does sum + r.minutes with no coercion, and the render uses Number(r.minutes). Driven: stored [{name:'Old soup',minutes:'20'},{name:'No time'},{name:'Num id',id:123,minutes:5}], then added New/10. Status read: "Total cooking time: 020undefined510 minutes." and the list showed "No time NaN min".
failing_case: Any saved record from an earlier shape (minutes as a string, minutes absent) makes the success message after every add show string-concatenated garbage instead of a number. The wrong total is shown as a confirmed result.
remediation: Normalise at the load boundary: require a string name, an id string (generate one if absent) and Number.isFinite(minutes) > 0 (coerce numeric strings), drop or repair the rest. Add a schema version to the saved shape.
